## Details ### Root Cause Profiling `_fwd_grouped_kernel_stage1` on H100 revealed two hardware bottlenecks: 1. **L2 Cache Thrashing Across Head Blocks:** With `grid = (batch, NUM_HEAD_BLOCKS, NUM_KV_SPLITS)`, CUDA launches CTAs along `grid[0]` (`batch`) first. For 128-head MLA (`NUM_HEAD_BLOCKS = 8`), all 8 head blocks for a given `(batch, kv_split)` share the exact same compressed KV cache pages (`cur_kv_head = 0`), but scheduling across `batch` first evicted those KV pages from L2 before the remaining head blocks for the same request ran. 2. **Uncoalesced Global KV Loads & Shared-Memory Bank Conflicts:** Loading `K_Buffer` in transposed `[BLOCK_DMODEL, BLOCK_N]` (`[512, 32]`) layout placed the strided token axis (`stride_buf_kbs`) on the inner warp-coalescing dimension. Adjacent threads jumped across separate token rows, yielding `21.3 / 32` byte sector utilization (`27%` excessive global sectors), forcing an in-register transpose with `4.4-way` shared-memory bank conflicts, and requiring `v = tl.trans(k)` on the MLA path. ### Design Decisions & Tradeoffs * **Co-schedule head blocks on `grid[0]`:** Swapping `grid` to `(NUM_HEAD_BLOCKS, batch, NUM_KV_SPLITS)` schedules all `NUM_HEAD_BLOCKS` sharing a KV slice concurrently on the SMs, raising L2 hit rates from `~55%` to `~74%` without altering output indexing or determinism. * **Row-major `[BLOCK_N, BLOCK_DMODEL]` KV loads:** Loading `k` and `kpe` with contiguous `offs_d[None, :]` on the inner dimension enables 128-bit vectorized loads (`LDG.E.128`), writes directly into native `K`-major shared-memory layouts for `tl.dot(q, tl.trans(k.to(q.dtype)))` without bank conflicts, and eliminates `tl.trans(k)` when `IS_MLA=True` (`v = k`). * **Scope:** Kept strictly to Stage-1 grid order and `K_Buffer` load layout so the existing two-stage reduction (`_fwd_kernel_stage2`), batch-invariant deterministic reduction order, and cross-platform support (CUDA, ROCm, XPU) remain intact with minimal code churn. ## Comments I dont have enough compute to test the kernel in E2E model like DSv3, etc. I tried benchmarking DSv2 Lite, but it only has 16 query heads due to which the perf delta was neglibible. I would appreciate if someone could test a bigger model E2E with this kernel patched up. Also appreciate kernel level and E2E benchmarking on other hardware (AMD, etc) that this triton MLA backend supports. first step of #69030: deprecate the torchao quantization backend, to be removed in v0.37.

## Overview

Let HY4 DFly run on compressed-tensors targets regardless of their layer scheme, enabling speculative decoding for [RedHatAI/Hy4-NVFP4](https://huggingface.co/RedHatAI/Hy4-NVFP4).

## Claims

- DFly accepts compressed-tensors HY4 targets with any layer scheme, rejecting only a `kv_cache_scheme` or non-empty transforms.
- An empty `transform_config: {}`, as serialized by compressed-tensors, is treated as no transforms.
- Draft layers are BF16 or blockwise W8A8 FP8, checked exactly.
- HY4 Flash's own checkpoint validation is unchanged.

## Validation

### Unit tests

```
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" python -m pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dfly_quantization.py -q
```

```
FAILED tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dfly_quantization.py::test_draft_scheme_is_restricted[int8]
3 failed, 3 passed, 16 warnings in 23.20s
```


| RedHatAI/Hy4-NVFP4 | rejected | accepted | 38 BF16 |
| tencent/Hy4-FP8 | accepted | accepted | 37 FP8, 1 BF16 |


</details>

### End to end on the full 770B model (4x B300, TP4), at `fc56c61ae0`

```
vllm serve <checkpoint> --tensor-parallel-size 4 --dtype bfloat16 --max-model-len 65536 \
  --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":0,"video":0}' --reasoning-parser hy_v4 \
  --attention-backend FLASHMLA_SPARSE \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dfly","num_speculative_tokens":5}'

lighteval endpoint litellm model.yaml "gsm8k_platinum|0" --custom-tasks custom_tasks.py --max-samples 300
```

`model.yaml` sets temperature 0.9, top_p 1.0, seed 0 and 64 concurrent requests. `gsm8k_platinum` is lighteval's `gsm8k` task pointed at `madrylab/gsm8k-platinum`, without the generation cap and stop sequence. Compiled extensions came from a precompiled build at `b24eda712`.

| RedHatAI/Hy4-NVFP4 | 289/300 | 288/300 | 2.955 |
| tencent/Hy4-FP8 | 295/300 | 292/300 | 2.939 |

"Without DFly" is main `4ae5147815` on the same questions, taken from full GSM8K Platinum runs at 100 to 128 concurrent requests. The FP8 DFly row was measured at `d6506619fd`. No speedup is claimed.

The model card's serve command for RedHatAI/Hy4-NVFP4, at its default 1M context, starts and serves at `fc56c61ae0` (KV cache 1,445,376 tokens).

### Coverage limits

- Target schemes other than NVFP4 and FP8 are covered only at config validation.
- DFly with image or video inputs on NVFP4 is unverified.
- CI cannot hold the 770B checkpoint, so end-to-end coverage is manual.
- The Read the Docs failure is also on main: the same 15 `docs/training/weight_updates` link warnings, starting at #69248.

## Details

**Root cause.** `adapt_draft_model_config` applied HY4 Flash's list of FP8 and MXFP4 checkpoint formats to every DFly target. DFly shares the target's MLA KV cache, indexer top-k, embedding and LM head, and does not depend on how the other layers are quantized. KV spec compatibility and BF16 embedding and head are already checked when the draft is loaded.

**Design.** For compressed-tensors, scheme support is left to the target model. Native FP8 checkpoints keep their existing check. Draft layers get their own exact check, matching what the draft loader reads.

**Out of scope.** Draft quantization beyond FP8: the DFly loader infers FFN width from `.weight` shapes and expects BF16 or FP8 dtypes, and the drafter is only 3.3B parameters.

**Related PRs.** I found no open PR for compressed-tensors NVFP4 targets with DFly.

- #68387 adds a separate `modelopt_fp4` bypass for HY4 Flash in the same function.
- #68839 copies the `num_bits`-only draft check into an AMD drafter, which will need the same exact check once this lands.
